_comment: Declarative UI-screen configuration shared across implementations. This describes screen chrome (headers, menus, difficulty rows) so the pygame (Python) and Three.js (TypeScript) front-ends can be kept in sync from one source instead of hand-matching layouts. Board geometry lives elsewhere (see docs/plans/typescript-rewrite-same-repo.md); this file is UI only. Schema: web/src/config/screens.ts.
_themeComment: Chrome palettes, ported from the pygame THEMES registry (minesweeper/gui.py) so both front-ends offer the same looks; tests/test_theme_sync.py guards the two against drift. Field names follow the web's CSS custom properties, which do NOT map one-to-one onto the pygame keys: `panel` is the card fill (pygame `button`) and `counterBg` is the dark LED box (pygame `panel`). A colour may carry an alpha suffix (#rrggbbaa) where the web look needs one. `dark` and `classicDark` are web-only — all six pygame presets are light, and those two are the dark halves of a pair: a theme (web/src/ui/theme.ts) names one palette per colour scheme, so `ios`/`dark` and `classic`/`classicDark` are the two pairs it composes.

hud._comment: Header row: left cluster, centred status cluster, right cluster. Slots are rendered left-to-right within each cluster; a front-end shows only the slots it supports at a given board. The two side clusters are kept the same size (two slots each) on purpose: the web header lays them out as equal grid columns either side of an auto-width centre, so an extra slot on one side alone wraps that column onto a second row while the other stays half empty.
hud._boardBarComment: Controls that belong to the board rather than to the game: they sit on the caption row under the header, beside the board's name, not in the header row itself. The header holds two slots a side and the centred status block, which is all that fits on one row on a phone; these are shown only on a board that has them, so putting them there would wrap that row on exactly the boards that have the most to fit.
hud._symmetryComment: One control per symmetry the board carries (boards/symmetry.ts BoardSymmetry). The ids are named for a wrapped surface, whose two directions are round the ring and round the tube, and carry over to the other two kinds: a flat board is the window such a surface is cut from, so its x is the ring and its y the tube, and on a solid `ring` and `tube` are rotations about the board's principal axis and one across it. The labels say what the control does to the board rather than naming a seam, because one label has to serve all three. `symmetry:<id>` shows a control on a board that has that symmetry at all; `symmetry-pair:<id>` shows the second of a pair only where the symmetry is not its own inverse. A reflection always is one -- `keepSymmetries` drops a candidate mirror that is not -- and so is a Klein bottle's half-tube step, so those get a single button where a translation gets two.
